method: Opened all seven chapter reference targets and inspected relevant passages. Individual official sign captions/artwork reused from the verified register with hash and size checks; not a claim that every individual sign page was fetched again.

sources.finding: Right-hand priority applies when vehicle paths cross, including three-way junctions and parking areas; general care duties remain. Special duties retained from Traffic Regulation §21.

Chapter 3 §§18–29, 43–44 and 60–66 checked: exit rule, priority-road/no-lane-change exception, roundabout entry, acceleration-lane join, turning position, mutual adaptation, controlled/uncontrolled crossings and signalling. Current provisions used; unrelated future amendments not applied. The short acceleration-lane companion explanation is explicitly sourced to §23.
Uncontrolled pedestrian-crossing duties, walking a bicycle versus riding, and controlled-crossing distinction confirmed.
Pedestrian rules apply to wheelchair use at walking speed, irrespective of propulsion; no wider classification inferred.

Marked cycle passage differs from cycle crossing. Cycle crossing requires markings/signs and design securing no more than 30 km/h. Drivers yield to riders on/about to enter; riders consider approaching traffic. After-turn/roundabout-exit passage duty checked in Traffic Regulation §61.

Official guide confirms anticlockwise travel, entry yield, lane choice according to signs/markings, no signal solely for entry, safe signalled lane changes and right signal on exit. Extra room for long vehicles is preserved.
TSFS 2011:20 chapter 3 §3 supports reflective self-assessment; chapter 3 §2 supports observation, interaction, safety margins and consequence assessment.

G4_sources.version: Live official driver manual; publication/update date not displayed in inspected passage
G4_sources.locator: Right-of-Way: left-turn example immediately after the opposite-direction arrival bullet; wheels-straight and completion sentences
G4_sources.excerpt: Keep your wheels straight to prevent being pushed into oncoming traffic if your vehicle is hit from behind.
G4_sources.supports: Keep wheels straight while waiting to turn left across oncoming traffic; rear impact can push a pre-steered vehicle into the opposing path; turn when it can safely be completed.
G4_sources.fallback_reason: Exact technique and rear-impact explanation not located through inspected TS/TRV searches. Direct government driver teaching is an appropriate fallback for this shared driving technique.
G4_sources.scope_limits: Safety advice, not presented as a separately established Swedish statutory wheel-angle duty. Only wheel position and its risk explanation are used; New York right-of-way, junction-entry, signal and other legal instructions are not imported. Straight wheels reduce a risk, not guarantee protection.
G4_sources.retrieval_method: Direct primary government web page retrieved and exact passage inspected
